comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
rebar-debug Phase 1 COMPLETE — root cause confirmed, mechanism observed at runtime.

PROVEN ROOT CAUSE
The in-process library read path has no initialization guard. `_reads._tracker()`
(_reads.py:31-33) resolves the tracker dir and returns it unchecked; all 7 read entries
(_reads.py:61,82,129,139,149,168,184) funnel through it. The actual masking happens one
layer down at reducer/_api.py:257-260, which wraps `os.listdir(tracker_path)` in
`except OSError: return results` — FileNotFoundError IS an OSError, so a missing tracker
directory yields `[]` rather than an error.

DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENT (purely local; no network, no proxy, no AWS)
Same uninitialized store, same library, same process:
  rebar.list_tickets(repo_root=tmp)   -> []                       (SILENT)
  rebar.create_ticket(..., tmp)       -> RebarError "ticket system not initialized"
  rebar list (CLI)                    -> Error: not initialized, exit 1
Reads and writes DISAGREE about whether an absent store is an error. This kills the
"intended behavior" alternative: the codebase plainly treats an uninitialized store as an
error condition; only the read path fails to say so. Scope measured: list_tickets, search,
and recent_session_logs all return [] silently; show_ticket raises but with the WRONG cause
("Ticket '<id>' not found" instead of "store not initialized").

The guard exists on every sibling surface and is missing on exactly one:
  CLI reads      _engine_support/reads_cli.py:340,384   -> guards, exit 1
  library writes _store/event_prepare.py:99-102          -> guards, RebarError
  library reads  _reads.py                                -> NO GUARD  <-- the defect

PRODUCTION IMPACT (how this was found)
The deployed MCP server at https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp reports "Connected" and
answers list_tickets/search/ready_tickets with [], show_ticket with "ticket_not_found", while
fsck reports "ticket system not initialized (/app/.tickets-tracker not found)"
(_commands/fsck.py:263-267 — the only tool that checks). The container genuinely has no
store; that provisioning gap is a SEPARATE defect filed alongside this one. This ticket is
the reason the gap is invisible: an agent following the MCP-first tracker rule is told
"no tickets" instead of "store missing", and files duplicates.

AUTHORITY VIOLATED (why this is a defect, not intended behavior)
- docs/mcp-reference.md:7 — MCP faults surface as distinct error codes "instead of silently
  resolving to a fallback", so "a driving agent can tell a broken config from a deliberate
  policy refusal". Returning [] for a missing store defeats exactly that contract.
- In-repo precedent that this failure CLASS is a defect: bug spiny-ferry-ripen (a filter that
  "returns [] with exit 0 — indistinguishable from 'no tickets match'", quoted at
  reads_cli.py:325-328) and bug bilingual-capitalist-caecilian ("Silent data-hiding: no error
  is surfaced to the operator; the store simply looks empty").

DEFECT ORIGIN — attributed to tend-tomb-doe (df9b-663a-98ed-4dc4), NOT by blame majority
Introducing commit 7d53bc5b43b7 (2026-06-09), "feat(reads): in-process native library reads
behind REBAR_NATIVE_READS (#2 Steps 0/2/3)". It created the second read path, claiming to
replicate "each shim's exact contract", while stating in the same message:
  "Deliberate behavior change: in-process reads do not run the dispatcher's
   _ensure_initialized — they are pure local replay."
The drop was framed as being about the git-fetch, but _ensure_initialized also carried the
not-initialized signal, so the guard silently left the read path. Its parity test
(tests/interfaces/test_native_read_parity.py) covered an *empty* store but never an
*uninitialized* one; 28406790c61e later deleted that test as "now-moot", and no test asserts
uninitialized-store read behavior today.

Attribution note — I am NOT naming the commit a whole-file blame would name. `git blame` on
_reads.py points at later refactors (f0bae9dec78b, ad30433f3443) that only moved the
unguarded code around; those are carriers. 7d53bc5b43b7 is where the behavior became wrong.
The commit predates the rebar-ticket trailer convention, so the ticket was recovered by
tracker search on the changed behavior: tend-tomb-doe, "#2 Step 3: wire public reads behind
REBAR_NATIVE_READS kill-switch", whose own scope was "Map in-process exceptions to existing
RebarError/ConcurrencyError shapes" with AC "parity tests green both ways". The uninitialized
case was never mapped and never tested — an unmet obligation a reviewer on that ticket could
plausibly have caught. close_class will be plan_defect.

CALLER-DEPENDENCY GATE: CLEARED
All _reads consumers are the public facade in _lib_reads.py plus llm/completion.py and
llm/spec_scan.py (show_ticket, which already raises). Callers that legitimately tolerate a
missing tracker already guard it themselves (mcp_server.py:760, next_batch.py:153), so none
depend on [] for an absent store.

FIX SEAM: the guard goes at _reads._tracker(), the one chokepoint the 7 read entries share —
the read-side mirror of event_prepare._ensure_initialized. An initialized-but-empty store
still returns [] (the directory exists), so the no-regression AC holds by construction.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Plan review: PASS (0 blocking, 4 advisory), model bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6.
Dispositions for all four advisories:

E1 + E3 (apply-now, priority 1.0) — "AC1 omits ready_tickets although the Impact section names
it as one of the silently-empty reads". ACCEPTED AND FIXED. This was a real under-coverage: the
Impact section lists `list_tickets / search / ready_tickets -> []` but AC1 enumerated only
list_tickets, search, recent_session_logs. AC1 is amended to read:

  AC1: A library read — `list_tickets`, `search`, `ready`, `recent_session_logs` (the MCP tool
  spelling of `ready` is `ready_tickets`) — against a repo with no tracker directory raises the
  same not-initialized RebarError the write path raises, instead of returning [].

The regression test is extended to exercise `rebar.ready` alongside the other three. Because the
fix already existed in the tree when this gap was found, the added coverage was NOT simply
appended to a passing suite: the fix was reverted first, the strengthened test was re-verified
RED with no fix present, and only then was the fix re-applied — the test-modification ordering
the debug protocol requires.

E2 (deferred, priority 0.17) — "state the fix locus explicitly rather than leaving it inferable".
ACCEPTED as documentation. The locus is now stated in the code itself: the guard lives at the
single `_reads._tracker()` funnel point, so all seven read entries inherit it uniformly; the ACs
sample the user-visible ones rather than enumerating internals.

G6 (deferred, priority 0.52) — "the two cited parity targets use DIFFERENT guard predicates; the
plan does not say which the new guard uses". ACCEPTED as a real ambiguity, and resolved
deliberately AGAINST the reviewer's suggested fix. The facts are correct:

  write path    event_prepare.py:101   isdir(tracker) AND exists(tracker/.git)
  CLI read path reads_cli.py:340       isdir(tracker) only

The reviewer suggested adopting the stronger write-path predicate "for true read/write parity".
We deliberately chose `isdir` only, matching the CLI READ path, because:

1. The surface being brought into parity is the READ surface. The defect was that library reads
   disagreed with CLI reads; matching `reads_cli.py:340` closes exactly that gap. Adopting the
   write predicate would make library reads STRICTER than CLI reads and open a NEW divergence in
   the opposite direction — trading one asymmetry for another.
2. A tracker directory that exists WITHOUT `.git` is a real, supported read case in this repo,
   not a hypothetical. `tests/unit/test_store_copy_needs_env_id.py` documents a store
   materialised by `git archive` of the orphan `tickets` branch: writes are refused on it while
   reads are expected to work. A `.git`-requiring read guard would break that fixture and the
   J11 live-DC cells that depend on it.
3. The write path's extra `.git` check exists to protect event APPENDS (provenance stamping),
   which has no read-side analogue.

So the divergence between the two predicates is intentional and load-bearing, not an oversight —
reads and writes legitimately answer different questions about the same directory. Recorded here
rather than as an ADR (the E2 coaching move suggested one) because this is a restatement of
existing behavior, not a one-way door.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
rebar-debug COMPLETE — Phase 2 landed for review as Gerrit change 2226.

TEST (held out from the fix subagent)
tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py, 7 cases.
- Proven RED first, for the RIGHT reason: 6 failed / 1 passed with no fix present. The four
  list-shaped reads and the parity case failed "DID NOT RAISE RebarError"; show_ticket failed
  on blaming the id. The 1 pass was the no-regression case, which is what proves the oracle
  discriminates rather than just rejecting everything.
- GREEN after the fix: 7/7, against a file the fix subagent never saw. The test was physically
  moved OUT of its worktree before it was launched, and its prompt named the path as off-limits;
  it received only the mechanism and the contract, never the assertions.
- Has teeth (mutation check): re-introducing the exact confirmed defect — deleting the isdir
  guard so `_tracker` returns the path unchecked — returned the suite to 6 failed; restoring the
  guard returned it to 7 passed.
- Not a change-detector: every assertion is on observable behavior (raised type + message), none
  on a private name, an intermediate value, or a grep of source text.

FIX
src/rebar/_reads.py, +12/-2. The guard goes at `_tracker()`, the single chokepoint the seven
library read entries share — the read-side mirror of `event_prepare._ensure_initialized`. It
keys on the tracker DIRECTORY's existence, so an initialized-but-empty store still reads `[]`.
`reducer/_api.py`'s `except OSError` is deliberately left alone: other callers rely on that
low-level tolerance, so the fault is named at the library read boundary instead.

Note the fix subagent was stopped mid-verification after ~30 minutes and the validation above was
run directly. That does not weaken the held-out property: the diff had been frozen in the tree
for 30 minutes at that point, and the subagent never had access to the oracle at any stage, so
there was no path by which it could tailor to it. Only its self-check was cut short, and every
check it would have run was then re-run here.

SCOPE & SAFETY
- Caller-dependency gate: CLEARED. All `_reads` consumers are the public facade plus
  llm/completion.py and llm/spec_scan.py (show_ticket, which already raised). Callers that
  legitimately tolerate a missing tracker already guard it themselves (mcp_server.py:760,
  next_batch.py:153). Nothing depended on `[]` for an absent store.
- Restoration, not creation: the guard restores parity that already exists on the CLI read path
  and the write path. No new command, artifact, or external call.
- No new dependency: uses the already-imported `os` and the existing `_rebar_error` helper.
- No test weakened: the only pre-existing file touched is `_reads.py`; the test file is purely
  additive.

REGRESSION EVIDENCE
13,697 passed / 45 skipped on tests/unit. Five ERRORs appeared, all of them the same repo-hygiene
watchdog ("New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT: ['.ruff_cache']") tripped by my own concurrent
`make lint` run, NOT by this change. Re-run clean after removing `.ruff_cache`: 114/114 passed.
`make lint` (incl. the complexity ratchet and module-size gate) and `make typecheck` (660 files)
both clean.

SIBLINGS — Step 7, both axes
Axis 1 (construct sweep): the root cause is a single missing guard at one chokepoint, not a
repeatable construct, so there is no construct to sweep for. Not swept, deliberately.
Axis 2 (parity census) — the rule: "a read against a non-existent tracker must report the missing
store". Five slots:
  1 CLI command        GUARDED    reads_cli.py:340,384
  2 MCP tool           GUARDED    inherits via _mcp_reads -> rebar.list_tickets
  3 library facade     GUARDED    this fix
  4 automated callers  MISSING    impossible_links.py:182 and relation_snapshot.py:257 call
                                  reduce_all_tickets directly, bypassing the boundary
  5 dual-direction     GUARDED    event_prepare.py:99-102 (writes)
Slot 4 disposition: ticket FILED, not fixed in scope — brigandish-weepy-amurminnow
(cecb-5a41-b8ca-4957), linked discovered_from this bug. Both callers run against a store already
established by the time they execute, so this is a latent parity gap rather than a reachable
failure; folding it in would have widened a proven single-site fix into a speculative one.

REPLICATION
The original report reproduces no longer. Against a store with no tracker directory, all five
public reads now raise "ticket system not initialized" — `list_tickets`, `search`, `ready`,
`recent_session_logs`, and `show_ticket` (which now blames the store, not the id) — matching what
`fsck` has always reported. An initialized-but-empty store still reads `[]`.

RESIDUAL RISK — observed with citations, each dispositioned
- Slot 4 above — TICKET FILED (cecb-5a41-b8ca-4957).
- The public `rebar.reduce_all_tickets` export (__init__.py:143,235) keeps the same silent-[]
  property — ACCEPTED: it is the low-level primitive and its tolerance is relied upon; the
  guard belongs at the boundary above it.
- `tests/interfaces` was not run to completion in this session (the subagent's run was cut short
  at ~30 min and only tests/unit was re-run) — ACCEPTED: CI's Verified gate runs the full suite
  on change 2226, and this change touches one private function on the read path.

THE PRODUCTION FAULT THIS EXPOSED IS SEPARATE AND STILL OPEN
This ticket fixes only the MASKING. The deployed server's store is still absent, and its cause is
an infra omission tracked separately: kilted-nuclear-bronco (mcp service never provisions a
store), mobile-groovy-badger (/health cannot see the store, so a storeless deploy passes the
readiness gate), receptive-houndy-nilgai (autodeploy AuthConfigError crash-loop, alarm firing,
live fix un-versioned). After this change the server will report the fault loudly instead of
answering "no tickets", but it will not have tickets until kilted-nuclear-bronco is resolved.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Patchset 3 (Gerrit 2226) addresses the second LLM-Review -1.

FINDING (valid, and a genuine miss in my caller sweep): rebar.audit.server._audited_tickets
calls the PUBLIC rebar.list_tickets uncaught, so the new RebarError propagated out of a
read-only web index handler — a page that should render empty now 500s. My Phase-1
caller-dependency gate searched `_reads.*` consumers and therefore never saw this call site,
which reaches the same code through the public facade. The sweep was aimed at the wrong symbol.

FIX: the enumeration is guarded for the uninitialized-store case only, restoring the function's
own documented contract ('Best-effort: audit_trail never raises'). Every OTHER read failure
still propagates, so a genuinely broken store is not silently blanked. Regression test added
(test_audit_index_renders_empty_rather_than_500ing_without_a_store) and mutation-checked: it
goes RED when the guard is removed.

RE-RAN THE SWEEP PROPERLY, on the public names this time. The remaining callers are
llm/code_review/{finalize,sidecar,fp_ledger}.py and audit/read.py:163. audit/read.py is already
inside a broad `except Exception` so it is unaffected; the code_review paths run only where a
store necessarily exists (you cannot run a code review without one). audit/server.py was the
only exposed caller.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CI Verified -1 on all four changes in this stack was NOT caused by any of them. Root-caused
rather than rechecked, per the flaky-test rule; recording it here because it will hit anyone
else with an open patchset right now.

SIGNATURE: only the macos-latest/py3.13 cell failed; all three ubuntu cells passed. pytest
exited 5 ('no tests collected') with 'no tests ran in 55.52s' — no collection error, no
traceback, no timeout.

MECHANISM — a workflow/tree skew. The Verified lane resolves the reusable workflow from
TRUSTED main (Uses: _build-and-test.yml@refs/heads/main) while checking out the PATCHSET's
tree. Commit 920492b1b2f7 ('Reduce macOS pytest cell to platform-compat subset') split its
contract across both halves: the workflow now passes -m 'platform_compat and not external'
(_build-and-test.yml:652), but the marker is auto-applied at collection time by a path-fragment
table in tests/conftest.py:198-252 — which lives in the TREE. Any patchset whose parent
predates that merge therefore gets a workflow asking for a marker no test in its tree can
carry: empty selection, exit 5.

EVIDENCE it is not the change: 6 recent macOS jobs show exit 5 across FOUR unrelated Gerrit
changes (fix(reads), Pin ticket reads, fix(autodeploy), feat(mcp)); ZERO macOS jobs exited 5
before 920492b1b2f7 merged at ~02:04 UTC. The fault tracks that merge time, not any
patchset's content. This stack was based on 95387192861c — the commit immediately before it.

REMEDY: rebase, NOT recheck. A recheck re-runs the same stale tree and fails identically.
Rebased all four onto origin/main 537456586d45; the macOS selection now collects 909 tests
instead of 0, confirming both the diagnosis and the fix. Re-verified on the new base: 110/110
of the affected tests pass, make lint and make typecheck clean.

WORTH NOTING FOR THE OWNERS OF 920492b1b2f7: the parity guard that change advertises
(test_ci_workflow_parity.py) also lives in the tree, so it cannot fire on a patchset that
predates it — the guard is blind to exactly the skew it exists to catch. Not filing a ticket
against it from here since it is outside this bug's scope, but it will keep biting every open
change until each is rebased.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Patchset 5 (Gerrit 2226) answers all three findings with one design change rather than three patches.

BLOCKING (api-compat): 'public/MCP reads now RAISE for a previously-valid case'. The finding
is correct — this IS a breaking change to a public surface, and it is the point of the ticket.
What was missing is what makes a breaking change *usable*: a way for a consumer to tell THIS
fault apart from every other read failure. Added:
  - a new stable code `store_uninitialized` in rebar.KNOWN_ERROR_CODES, set via the existing
    exc.error_code seam (_errors.error_code_for precedence 5), so it surfaces over the MCP
    error envelope rather than collapsing into `command_failed`;
  - a CHANGELOG [Unreleased]/Changed entry with an explicit migration line: a caller that
    relied on the empty-list degrade catches RebarError and branches on
    error_code_for(exc) == 'store_uninitialized'; an INITIALIZED-but-empty store still returns
    [] unchanged, so only the missing-store case is affected.
This is the same principle docs/mcp-reference.md:7 already states for config faults — surface a
distinct code 'instead of silently resolving to a fallback', so a driving agent can tell a
broken environment from a legitimate result. Verified end-to-end: the code is emitted, is in
KNOWN_ERROR_CODES, and is distinct from command_failed.

ADVISORY (maintainability): the audit guard matched the substring 'not initialized', coupling
audit.server to wording defined in four other modules. Fixed by the same change — it now
matches error_code_for(exc) == 'store_uninitialized'. The reviewer was right that the string
was the wrong seam; it was a stopgap and is gone.

ADVISORY (tests): the re-raise branch was untested. Added
test_audit_index_still_propagates_a_non_store_read_failure — a RebarError carrying
command_failed must propagate, not degrade. Without it a future 'simplification' to a bare
`except RebarError: return []` would reintroduce the exact silent-empty failure this ticket
removes, just relocated into the audit server. That is the more valuable half of the guard.

113 affected tests green; make lint and make typecheck clean.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The in-process library read path (`rebar._reads`) has **no initialization guard**, so every
read against a repo whose tracker directory does not exist returns an EMPTY result with no
error. The CLI read path guards this exact condition
(`_engine_support/reads_cli.py:340-342` -> "ticket system not initialized", exit 1), and the
library WRITE path guards it too (`_store/event_prepare.py:99-102`), but the library/MCP READ
path does not.

Because the MCP read tools delegate straight to the library (`_mcp_reads.py:295` ->
`rebar.list_tickets`), an MCP client pointed at a host with a missing store is told
"there are no tickets" instead of "this store is not initialized".

## Impact (observed in production)

The deployed rebar MCP server at `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` has no
`/app/.tickets-tracker`. It reports "Connected" and answers:

- `list_tickets` / `search` / `ready_tickets` -> `[]`   (silent)
- `show_ticket <real alias>`                  -> "ticket_not_found"  (loud but WRONG cause)
- `fsck`                                      -> "ticket system not initialized (/app/.tickets-tracker not found)"  (correct)

An agent following the repo's MCP-first tracker rule therefore sees an empty tracker,
concludes no ticket exists for its work, and files duplicates -- the precise
silent-data-hiding failure mode already recorded as a defect for the store-divergence case
in bug bilingual-capitalist-caecilian ("Silent data-hiding: no error is surfaced to the
operator; the store simply looks empty") and for the filter case in bug spiny-ferry-ripen.

## Authoritative sources violated

- `docs/mcp-reference.md:7` -- MCP faults are surfaced as distinct error codes "instead of
  silently resolving to a fallback", so "a driving agent can tell a broken config from a
  deliberate policy refusal". `[]` for a missing store defeats exactly this.
- Surface parity: the CLI (`reads_cli.py:340`) and library writes (`event_prepare.py:99`)
  both raise on this condition; library reads alone do not.

## Root cause

`_reads.py` resolves the tracker through `_tracker()` (`_reads.py:31-33`) and never checks
that the directory exists; all 8 read entries funnel through it unguarded.

Origin: commit 7d53bc5b43b7 (2026-06-09, "#2 Steps 0/2/3") introduced the in-process read
path, stating it replicated "each shim's exact contract" while explicitly noting the
in-process reads "do not run the dispatcher's `_ensure_initialized`". Its parity test
covered an *empty* store but never an *uninitialized* one; that test was later deleted as
"now-moot" by 28406790c61e. Ticket: tend-tomb-doe (df9b-663a-98ed-4dc4), whose own scope was
"Map in-process exceptions to existing RebarError shapes" + "parity tests green both ways".

## Reproduction (purely local, no network)

    tmp=$(mktemp -d); cd "$tmp"; git init -q .
    python3 -c "import rebar; print(rebar.list_tickets(repo_root='$tmp'))"   # -> []      (silent)
    python3 -c "import rebar; rebar.create_ticket('task','x',repo_root='$tmp')"  # -> RebarError: not initialized
    rebar list                                                              # -> Error: not initialized, exit 1

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A library read (`list_tickets`, `search`, `recent_session_logs`) against a repo with no
      tracker directory raises the same not-initialized `RebarError` the write path raises,
      instead of returning `[]`.
- [x] `show_ticket` against an uninitialized store reports the store as uninitialized rather
      than the misleading "Ticket '<id>' not found".
- [x] The corresponding MCP read tools surface that fault as a machine-readable error
      envelope, not an empty array.
- [x] An INITIALIZED-but-empty store still returns `[]` with no error (no regression).
- [x] Regression coverage asserts read/write parity on an uninitialized store.

## Scope of the read/write agreement — the predicates DIFFER, deliberately

Earlier wording in this plan claimed "read/write parity" without qualification. That overstates
it, and plan review was right to block on the claim. Stated precisely:

Reads and writes now agree that an **ABSENT tracker directory** is an error. They deliberately
do NOT agree about a directory that EXISTS but is not a git repo:

    write path   _store/event_prepare.py   isdir(tracker) AND exists(tracker/.git)
    CLI reads    _engine_support/reads_cli.py:340,384   isdir(tracker) only
    library reads  _reads._tracker (this change)        isdir(tracker) only

The read guard matches the CLI READ path, not the write path, and that is the correct target:
the defect was that library reads disagreed with CLI reads. Adopting the write predicate would
make library reads STRICTER than CLI reads — trading one asymmetry for a new one — and would
break a live, supported case.

Verified empirically on a tracker whose `.git` was removed (the shape a `git archive` of the
orphan `tickets` branch produces, documented in `tests/unit/test_store_copy_needs_env_id.py`):

    tracker dir exists: True | .git present: False
      READ  -> 1 ticket(s): reads WORK
      WRITE -> refused: "ticket system not initialized"

So reads on a `.git`-less store are working behavior that real fixtures depend on, not an
oversight. The write path's extra `.git` check guards event APPENDS (provenance stamping) and
has no read-side analogue.

The regression test is named for what it actually asserts —
`test_reads_and_writes_agree_that_an_absent_store_is_an_error` — i.e. the absent-directory case
only. No test claims the broader parity.

file_impact.reason: The guard at the single _tracker() chokepoint all seven library read entries funnel through, mirroring the write path _ensure_initialized
Add store_uninitialized to KNOWN_ERROR_CODES so the fault is machine-readable over the MCP envelope instead of requiring message-text matching (code review api-compat finding)
The one caller that legitimately depended on the old degrade-to-empty: the read-only audit web index must render empty rather than 500, scoped to the store_uninitialized code (code review finding)
Regression coverage: every guarded read raises, initialized-but-empty still returns [], read/write parity, audit index degrades, non-store failures still propagate
Update the expectation that asserted reads return [] without init, keeping the no-silent-creation invariant the file exists to protect
Pin the cross-interface library arm to the fixture store via the file own _pin helper; it was never scoped, and passed only because a missing store also yielded ticket_not_found
Record the intended public-surface change (the new error code) via the sanctioned gen_api_surface.py --update
Document the behavior change and the migration path for callers that relied on the empty-list degrade

compiled_state.title: Library and MCP reads mask an uninitialized store as an empty one (list/search/ready return [] instead of erroring)
